sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 1031 of 2023

Applicant :- Hukum Chand
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1. Heard Sri Kameshwar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and
perused the record.

2. This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant- Hukum Chand seeking anticipatory
bail in Case Crime No.634 of 2018, under sections- 420, 465, 468, 471 I.P.C. and sections- 3/7
Essential Commodities Act and section- 66D of I.T. Act and section- 34 The Aadhaar (Targeted
Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, Police Station- Civil Line,
District- Muzaffar Nagar.

entities.text:
Aadhaar (Targeted
Delivery of Financial and other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, Police Station- Civil Line,
District- Muzaffar Nagar
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3.  As per allegations in the F.I.R., a number of persons whose names and details have been given in the F.I.R. itself and the present applicant who were running the fair price shop, interpolated the software of the EPOS machine (through which the beneficiaries are identified by applying biometric methods) and distributed the rations to persons not entitled for the same; therefore, the F.I.R. is lodged under sections- 420, 467, 468 I.P.C. and sections- 3/7 Essential Commodities Act and section- 66D of I.T. Act against the ration dealers.
4.

It is contended on behalf of the applicant that he is innocent and has not carried out any manipulation in the EPOS machine; he does not possess any technical expertise to indulge and carry out any manipulation in such an equipment; he has been implicated by the authorities to save their own skin and to save the Government officials involved in the same.
5.

The application for anticipatory bail is opposed by the learned A.G.A. pointing out the fact that in Hukum Chand vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100710846/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 this case the applicant stands charge-sheeted in the year 2021.

6. In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion at any stage of the case based on material before him.

Order Date :- 22.3.2023 Saif  Hukum Chand vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100710846/
